name: Hoshea
overview: Hoshea was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, known primarily as the chief officer for the Ephraimites. He is identified as the son of Azaziah, highlighting his leadership role within his tribal community as recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:20. There are no additional notes or distinctions provided beyond his tribal affiliation and office.
namesAndTitles: The name Hoshea means 'salvation,' reflecting a proper Hebrew name without indication that it was given directly by God. This meaning aligns with the biblical emphasis on deliverance and God's saving power, though the text does not elaborate further on the significance of his name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hoshea was the son of Azaziah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 27:20. Beyond this paternal relationship, there are no other family connections mentioned in the biblical text for Hoshea.
scriptureSignificance: Hoshea's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his leadership position as chief officer of the Ephraimites, a key tribal group in Israel. His role indicates a level of responsibility and authority within the structure of Israelite society during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles. Although the text does not provide further narrative details, his inclusion underscores the organized tribal governance under God's providence.
